items.name: Car seat that fits baby's age and size
items.note: Correctly installed every time. The #1 safety item for any car journey.

variants.note: Only if you'll drive, rent a car or take taxis at your destination. Some rental firms and taxi services can provide one — book ahead.

items.name: Travel health insurance with infant cover
items.note: Many standard policies exclude babies under 8 weeks. Double-check yours.

items.name: Baby's passport (if travelling internationally)
items.note: Takes 4–6 weeks to process — apply early. Newborns need their own.

items.name: Vaccination record copy
items.note: Some destinations and paediatricians require these on arrival.

items.name: Formula + extra supply (if formula-feeding)
items.note: Bring 30% more than you think you need. Brands vary abroad.

items.name: Nursing cover / portable privacy wrap
items.note: Optional — but helpful in busy airports and restaurants.

items.name: Bottles + portable steriliser
items.note: A microwave steam bag works in most hotel rooms.

items.name: A feed ready for take-off and landing
items.note: Breast, bottle or dummy — sucking and swallowing can help with ear pressure.

variants.note: A drink with a straw or spout, or a chewy snack — swallowing can help with ear pressure.

items.name: Bibs × 6 minimum
items.note: You will always need more bibs than you think.

items.name: Snacks they already know and like
items.note: Pack more than seems reasonable. A hungry baby on the move is a meltdown waiting to happen.

items.name: Sippy cup or straw cup
items.note: Spill-resistant, and easier than a bottle once they're drinking water.

items.name: Nappies and wipes for the journey + first day
items.note: You can buy more at your destination — no need to fill a suitcase.

variants.name: Nappies and wipes for the whole trip
variants.note: For a short trip it's easiest to bring everything — plus a few spares for delays.

items.name: Portable changing mat
items.note: Some airports and restaurants lack changing facilities. Be prepared.

items.name: Nappy sacks or small rubbish bags
items.note: For dirty nappies and wet clothes when there's no bin in sight.

items.name: Spare outfits in your hand luggage
items.note: At least two for baby — and a spare top for you. Blowouts love a long journey.

items.name: Portable travel cot or book a hotel crib
items.note: Confirm with hotel 48h in advance. Specify infant, not toddler crib.

items.name: White noise app or portable speaker
items.note: Recreates home sleep sounds — powerful for unsettled environments.

items.name: Portable blackout blind
items.note: Clip-on, fits most windows. Game-changer for naps in bright rooms.

items.name: Baby's familiar sleep bag
items.note: Scent and feel of home. Huge comfort anchor for babies.

variants.name: Baby's familiar sleep bag or swaddle
variants.note: Scent and feel of home. If you swaddle, stop once baby shows signs of rolling.

items.name: Their favourite comfort toy (and a backup if you have one)
items.note: Losing it on day one is a trip-defining event. Keep it on a clip or in a known pocket.

items.name: Infant paracetamol (age-appropriate)
items.note: Check dosage weight-range on pack. Bring 2 bottles.

variants.note: Babies this young shouldn't be given medicine without advice. Ask your GP, pharmacist or health visitor what to bring before you go.

items.name: Digital thermometer
items.note: Ask your health visitor or pharmacist which type suits your baby's age.

items.name: Oral rehydration sachets (ORS)
items.note: For vomiting or diarrhoea — can't always find abroad. Check the pack for age guidance.

items.name: Nappy rash cream
items.note: Travel can trigger flare-ups from heat and different water.

items.name: Anti-bac wipes × 100+
items.note: Used for surfaces, tray tables, changing mats. Stock up.

items.name: Sunhat and stroller sunshade
items.note: Shade is the best sun protection for young babies — ask your pharmacist about sun cream for their age.

items.name: Check the airline's infant rules before you book
items.note: Lap-infant fares, bassinet seats, minimum age and what baby gear you can bring free all vary by airline.

items.name: A change of clothes for you in hand luggage
items.note: Spit-up and spills don't stay on the baby.

items.name: Plan regular breaks out of the car seat
items.note: Commonly advised: stop at least every 2 hours so baby can stretch out of the seat. Build them into your route.

items.name: Window sunshades for the car
items.note: Keeps direct sun off baby on long drives.

items.name: Rear-facing seat mirror
items.note: So the front-seat adult can glance at baby without turning round.

items.name: Reserve seats near the baby-change or with a table
items.note: A table seat gives you space to feed and change; near the end of the carriage gives you room to walk.

items.name: A few small new toys or books
items.note: Something new holds attention far longer than old favourites. Hand them out one at a time.

items.name: Downloaded shows or music
items.note: Downloaded, not streamed — signal disappears exactly when you need it. No guilt.

items.name: Lightweight stroller
items.note: Compact and easy to fold one-handed.

variants.name: Lightweight stroller (gate-check compatible)
variants.note: Ask at check-in — most airlines let you take it to the gate.

items.name: Baby carrier / sling
items.note: Hands-free and better than a stroller in crowds or cobblestones.

items.name: Nappy bag with packing cubes
items.note: Compartmentalise feed, change, sleep items. Saves you at 2am.

items.name: Travel wash or a place with a washing machine
items.note: On longer trips it's lighter to wash than to pack for every day.

items.name: Noise-cancelling earphones (yours!)
items.note: You deserve this. Especially on the return flight.
